title: Roll Back a Forwarder App through Reviewed Git History
objectives: Roll Back a Forwarder App through Reviewed Git History
Verify actual configuration, delivery and resulting operational behavior.

tasks.instruction: This isolated attempt starts paused. Use Forwarder Management to inspect clients/apps/classes, or Terminal SSH from the bastion. Linux UF: ssh splunk@lab-lnx-0001. Automation: ssh svc_ansible@ansible01 then cd ~/splunk-automation. Administrative changes and packages are entirely simulated.

The fixture deployed a bad canary app with sourcetype v7_broken. In ~/splunk-apps inspect git log/show and identify the non-merge Bad canary release fixture commit. Set a training Git name/email, create a recovery branch, revert that source commit and push. Open a PR, run checks, approve/merge, then Deploy the merged apps PR. Advance time and verify the recovered app and two explicit records in os. Direct target edits or rewriting history cannot replace the reviewed revert. After the client has activated the recovered catalog, append two fresh lines to /var/log/practice/forwarder.log on lab-lnx-0001 with practice_id=v7-recovery-001 and practice_id=v7-recovery-002. Advance again and verify those two new records. Data indexed with the prior bad sourcetype remains unchanged.

After the required activation, select the client in Forwarder Management and use Advance simulation 60 seconds. Inspect btool/forwarding output and independent Search as required. Record the evidence answer; an answer alone cannot complete the exercise.

hints: Distinguish staged source, published catalog, downloaded app and running configuration.
Use a narrow target and the component that owns the change. Inspect failures before retrying.

references.purpose: Predict changes, apply and verify idempotency

checks.label: Reviewed revert remains in deployed apps history
Verify actual forwarder lifecycle and delivery
Independent search finds only the explicit teaching records
